olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find all positive integers equal to 700 times the sum of their digits.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2012

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $\gamma$ = circumcircle of acute $\triangle ABC$; $P$ = midpoint of minor arc $BC$. Line through $P$ parallel to $AB$ meets $BC,AC,\gamma$ at $R,S,T$. $K=AP\cap BT$, $L=BS\cap AR$. Show $KL$ passes through the midpoint of $AB$ iff $CS=PR$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2012

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Equilateral triangle city of side 2012, divided into 1-cm equilateral triangles. 6036 streets total. Find the minimum number of sentinel sites (placed at intersections) to monitor every street.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2012

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Alexander and Louise: Louise steals $\frac{1}{3}$ of Alexander's money each morning, then gives him $\frac{1}{2}$ of all her money in the afternoon. Louise starts with no money. What is the minimum initial integer amount Alexander must have so both have integers after day 2012?
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2012

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $\triangle ABC$ with $AB<BC$; $E\in AC$, $F\in AB$ with $BF=BC=CE$. $G=BE\cap CF$. $H$ on the line through $G$ parallel to $AC$ with $HG=AF$ ($H,C$ on opposite sides of $BG$). Show $\angle EHG=\dfrac{\angle BAC}{2}$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2012
